When we measure “variation,” we are trying to answer the question “how spread out are the data?”
Other words that are synonymous with variation are “dispersion” and “spread.” When the data are close
together, we say that there is less variability, less dispersion, or are less spread out. Low variability,
then, means the data are more “consistent.” Data that are not grouped closely together are more spread
out, have higher variability, are widely dispersed, have more variation, and are less consistent. See
: Dot plots showing data with less variability and with more variability.
How much variation is in the data?
How spread out are the data?
How widely dispersed are the data?
